newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian police seize marijuana cargo.
newsitem.headline: Colombian police seize marijuana cargo.

text.p: Colombian police seized 37 tonnes of marijuana loaded aboard a Polish-registered ship in the Caribbean coast port of Cartagena on Saturday, authorities said.

Col. Leonardo Gallego, head of the counternarcotics division of the National Police, said the bust came after routine intelligence work. No arrests were made and it was not immediately apparent which of Colombia's powerful drug cartels had supplied the "giant" shipment, he said.

"We seized two containers with a giant cargo of marijuana, weighing a total 37 tonnes," Gallego told reporters in Cartagena. He said the cargo, which had been destined for Poland, would now be destroyed.

Colombia first gained international notoriety as a major supplier of drugs when it began exporting marijuana to the United States in the late 1960s and early 1970s, but the marijuana trade was quickly overtaken by the far more profitable cocaine business. Last year Colombian authorities seized more than 700 tonnes of purified or semi-processed cocaine and about 240 tonnes of marijuana.
U.S. anti-drug officials estimate Colombia supplies 80 percent of the world's cocaine and more recently has become the No.1 supplier of high-grade heroin to the United States.
